suppressions.message: Method called on moved-from object 'value' of type 'std::array'
suppressions.reason: CSA reports the reusable fixed-size nanobind array caster as moved-from at nb_array.h:34. Its from_python loop assigns every std::array element before extracting the completed value; the fixed-size array remains writable after the trivial element-wise move.
suppressions.reproducer: uv run python tools/native_checks.py --kind analyzer --build native/build; cplusplus.Move at native/src/rider/contact_binding.cpp:33 and nanobind/stl/detail/nb_array.h:34
suppressions.remove_when: Remove when CSA no longer emits this exact cplusplus.Move diagnostic at nb_array.h:34 for the contact_binding.cpp matrix conversion, or nanobind stops reusing the fixed-size element caster.

suppressions.reproducer: uv run cmake --build native/build --target check_tidy; clang-analyzer-cplusplus.Move at native/src/rider/contact_binding.cpp:33 and nanobind/stl/detail/nb_array.h:34
suppressions.remove_when: Remove when clang-tidy no longer emits this exact cplusplus.Move diagnostic at nb_array.h:34 for the contact_binding.cpp matrix conversion, or nanobind stops reusing the fixed-size element caster.

suppressions.message: Out of bound access to memory after the end of the field 'ob_item'
suppressions.reason: CSA flags PyTuple_GET_ITEM at nb_types.h:1583 as an out-of-bound read of ob_item, which CPython declares as a one-element array while tuple objects are allocated with variably sized storage; the iterator only walks indices < PyTuple_GET_SIZE.
suppressions.reproducer: uv run python tools/native_checks.py --kind analyzer --build native/build; security.ArrayBound at nanobind/nb_types.h:1583 reached via tuple iteration in native/src/runtime/runtime_binding.cpp owned_copy
suppressions.remove_when: Remove when CSA stops reporting PyTuple_GET_ITEM's variably sized ob_item access as out-of-bounds at nb_types.h:1583, or nanobind's tuple iterator stops using NB_TUPLE_GET_ITEM.

suppressions.message: Out of bound access to memory after the end of the field 'ob_item'
suppressions.reason: clang-tidy reports the same CSA false positive at PyTuple_GET_ITEM in nb_types.h:1583; PyTupleObject.ob_item is a single-element declaration whose storage is variably allocated per tuple length, and the seq_iterator only reads indices below the tuple size.
suppressions.reproducer: uv run cmake --build native/build --target check_tidy; clang-analyzer-security.ArrayBound at nanobind/nb_types.h:1583 reached via tuple iteration in native/src/runtime/runtime_binding.cpp owned_copy
suppressions.remove_when: Remove when clang-tidy no longer emits this exact ArrayBound diagnostic at nb_types.h:1583 for tuple iteration, or nanobind stops indexing ob_item through NB_TUPLE_GET_ITEM.

suppressions.message: Called C++ object pointer is uninitialized
suppressions.reason: Clang 18 CSA cannot model std::visit over the telemetry variant: it reports the freshly constructed nb::dict receiver inside the visitor lambda as an uninitialized object pointer at drive_binding.cpp:46 and :48. The variant `v` is bound to a live telemetry entry and `d` is a fully constructed nb::dict; the pinned LLVM 23 baseline does not emit this diagnostic.
suppressions.reproducer: cmake --build native/build-linux-clang --target check_analyzer; core.CallAndMessage at native/src/drivetrain/drive_binding.cpp:46 and :48 inside the std::visit dict writer
suppressions.remove_when: Remove when the Linux analyzer toolchain reaches a release that stops emitting this std::visit false positive for the dict writer.

suppressions.message: is within a recursive call chain
suppressions.reason: clang-tidy 18 misc-no-recursion cannot model std::visit dispatch through libstdc++'s std::variant internals and reports the libstdc++ variant operators themselves as recursive; the recursion through the recursive Wire variant is data-bounded and terminates. The pinned LLVM 23 baseline does not emit these diagnostics.

suppressions.remove_when: Remove when the Linux clang-tidy toolchain stops attributing std::visit recursion to libstdc++ variant internals.

suppressions.message: Use of memory after it is released
suppressions.reason: The read through `escaped[index]` at sanitizer_control.cpp:49 is the intentional injected defect of the T15 use-after-free control: the translation unit exists to prove the real ASan heap-use-after-free diagnostic fires in a fresh subprocess under the selected runtime. The defect must stay a true positive, so the analyzer record is suppressed in the manifest rather than NOLINT-ed, and the runtime control remains load-bearing evidence.
suppressions.reproducer: cmake --build native/build --target check_analyzer; cplusplus.NewDelete at native/tests/sanitizer_control.cpp:49 in use_after_free_control
suppressions.remove_when: Remove if the use-after-free control is deleted or rewritten so the escaped-pointer read no longer follows unique_ptr::reset.

suppressions.message: Use of memory after it is freed
suppressions.reason: Same intentional T15 defect as the pinned LLVM 23 record: `escaped[index]` at sanitizer_control.cpp:49 reads storage after unique_ptr::reset to produce the heap-use-after-free the ASan control subprocess must observe. The Ubuntu LLVM 18.1.3 analyzer on Linux emits the same diagnostic with 'freed' wording where LLVM 23 says 'released'.
suppressions.reproducer: cmake --build native/build-linux-clang --target check_analyzer; cplusplus.NewDelete at native/tests/sanitizer_control.cpp:49 in use_after_free_control
suppressions.remove_when: Remove if the use-after-free control is deleted or rewritten so the escaped-pointer read no longer follows unique_ptr::reset.
